page: The Microsoft Azure E2ps_v5 is an ARM64 virtual machine belonging to the EPSv5 server family, operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor delivering 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The processor cache configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not feature any local storage or integrated GPUs, though it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile, with single-core capabilities outperforming multi-core and memory-bound operations. In stress-ng single-core CPU tests and single-threaded gzip compression, the server achieved average performance. Conversely, multi-core stress-ng and single-threaded bzip3 decompression fell into the weak category. Memory bandwidth tests for both cached and uncached blocks, along with multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, registered in the poor category. Geekbench scores reflect these constraints, showing a single-core score of 1055.0 and a multi-core score of 1987.0.

The server exhibits performance tradeoffs in memory-intensive and parallelized tasks, with Passmark CPU and memory scores falling into the poor and weak categories respectively. Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput both placed in the bottom 10% of benchmarks. For AI workloads, LLM inference speed using a small 135M model was limited to 88.02 tokens per second for prompt processing and 27.36 tokens per second for text generation. Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8 coupled with modest compute capabilities, this server is qualitatively cost-efficient for lightweight, memory-intensive workloads such as small-scale caching, basic text processing, or lightweight development environments.
